source: Directive tables of the Bareos 25.1.2 Director as carried by odir (crates/odir/src/commands/show_items.rs) plus Onesimus extensions (crates/odir/src/config_check.rs EXTENSIONS)
description: A Pool resource groups volumes with the same rules: how long their data is kept, how big they get, how they are labeled and recycled.

examples.title: Full backups kept for a year on disk
examples.config:
Pool {
  Name = Full
  Pool Type = Backup
  Recycle = yes
  Auto Prune = yes
  Volume Retention = 365 days
  Maximum Volume Bytes = 50G
  Maximum Volumes = 100
  Label Format = "Full-"
  Action On Purge = Truncate
}

examples.title: Incrementals: one volume per job
examples.config:
Pool {
  Name = Incremental
  Pool Type = Backup
  Volume Retention = 30 days
  Maximum Volume Jobs = 1
  Label Format = "Incremental-"
}
examples.explanation: With one job per volume a volume can be recycled as soon as its single job has expired.

directives.name: Name
directives.description: Name of the pool.

directives.name: Description
directives.description: Free text describing the pool.

examples.console: configure add pool name=Full description="Full backups, kept one year"

directives.name: Pool Type
directives.description: Kind of pool: Backup (the normal case), Copy, Cloned, Archive, Migration or Scratch. Only Backup pools are used for backups; a pool named Scratch serves as the default scratch pool.

directives.name: Label Format
directives.description: Template for the names of volumes the Director labels automatically. Without it, volumes must be labeled by hand (label). The Director appends a 4-digit number unless the format uses variables such as ${NumVols}. For disk storage the Storage Daemon's device also needs Label Media = yes.

directives.name: Label Type
directives.description: Deprecated: ANSI or IBM tape labels.

directives.name: Cleaning Prefix
directives.description: Volumes whose name starts with this prefix are cleaning tapes and are never used for data.

directives.name: Use Catalog
directives.description: Keep the volumes of this pool in the catalog; should stay yes.

directives.name: Purge Oldest Volume
directives.description: When the pool needs a volume and none is free, purge the oldest volume regardless of its retention. Dangerous: data that should still be kept is lost.

directives.name: Action On Purge
directives.description: What happens to a volume when it is purged: Truncate shrinks a disk volume to zero to free the space (done by truncate or purge ... action=truncate); None keeps it.

directives.name: Recycle Oldest Volume
directives.description: When a volume is needed, prune the oldest volume and reuse it if its retention allows.

directives.name: Recycle Current Volume
directives.description: When a volume is needed, prune the current volume and reuse it if its retention allows.

directives.name: Maximum Volumes
directives.description: Upper limit of volumes in the pool; automatic labeling stops there. Together with Maximum Volume Bytes it caps the disk space of the pool.

directives.name: Maximum Volume Jobs
directives.description: Number of jobs after which a volume is marked Used. With 1, each job gets its own volume, which makes recycling of disk volumes precise.

directives.name: Maximum Volume Files
directives.description: Number of files after which a volume is marked Used.

directives.name: Maximum Volume Bytes
directives.description: Size after which a volume is marked Full. On disk storage this keeps volumes small enough to be recycled one by one. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

examples.console: configure add pool name=Full maximumvolumebytes="50 g"

directives.name: Catalog Files
directives.description: Store the file records of the jobs in this pool. Without them no single files can be selected for restore, only whole jobs.

directives.name: Volume Retention
directives.description: How long the jobs on a volume are kept after the volume was last written. When it has run out, the jobs and files on it can be pruned and the volume recycled. It is the main retention setting in Bareos 25. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

examples.console: configure add pool name=Full volumeretention="1 year"

directives.name: Volume Use Duration
directives.description: How long a volume is written to after its first write; then it is marked Used. Without it, a volume stays Append until it is full. Useful to get one volume per day or week. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

examples.console: configure add pool name=Full volumeuseduration="23 hours"

directives.name: Migration Time
directives.description: For Migrate jobs with Selection Type PoolTime: jobs older than this are migrated. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

examples.console: configure add pool name=Full migrationtime="30 days"

directives.name: Migration High Bytes
directives.description: For Selection Type PoolOccupancy: migration starts when the pool holds more than this. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

examples.console: configure add pool name=Full migrationhighbytes="800 g"

directives.name: Migration Low Bytes
directives.description: For Selection Type PoolOccupancy: migration stops when the pool is below this. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

examples.console: configure add pool name=Full migrationlowbytes="600 g"

directives.name: Next Pool
directives.description: Pool that Copy, Migrate and VirtualFull jobs write to when they read from this pool.

directives.name: Storage
directives.description: Storage the jobs writing to this pool use; it takes precedence over the Storage of the job.

directives.name: Auto Prune
directives.description: Prune the volumes of this pool automatically when a volume is needed, according to Volume Retention.

directives.name: Recycle
directives.description: Allow volumes of this pool to be reused once they are purged. With no, a full volume keeps its data until it is relabeled or deleted.

directives.name: Recycle Pool
directives.description: Pool a volume moves to when it is recycled, for example back to the Scratch pool.

directives.name: Scratch Pool
directives.description: Pool this pool takes new volumes from when it has none; default is the pool named Scratch.

directives.name: Catalog
directives.description: Catalog of the pool, for installations with several catalogs.

directives.name: File Retention
directives.description: Deprecated: file retention of the pool. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Job Retention
directives.description: Deprecated: job retention of the pool. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Minimum Block Size
directives.description: Minimum block size for volumes of this pool, for tape drives with special needs. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

examples.console: configure add pool name=Full minimumblocksize="64 k"

directives.name: Maximum Block Size
directives.description: Maximum block size for volumes of this pool; larger blocks speed up modern tape drives. Volumes written with one size must be read with it. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

examples.console: configure add pool name=Full maximumblocksize="1 m"
